title: Cluster 02 DRILL: Adaptive Immunity and Antibody Diversity
subtitle: H2 Biology 9477 · Book 9, Extension Topic A · 8 questions · 76 marks · 26 parts · one mark per minute, so a little over an hour and a quarter · every question is an actual exam paper question
intro_html:
Answers sit directly under each part, hidden. Click Show answer only after you have said your full reasoning aloud for that part. Check (a) before you start (b), that is the point of the layout.

Rate your confidence before every reveal. A dashed line sits above each answer block. Say high, medium or guessed out loud before you click. A right answer said hesitantly stays ACTIVE; a right answer said confidently moves on.

Every question below is a real exam paper question. The stem is the paper's own wording. Where a stem has been edited it is only so that it stands without the parts of the original that came before it, and the edit is written out in the Sources block at the foot of that question.

This cluster contains the highest-yield node in Book 9 and the single biggest trap in it. 9477 Specimen Paper 3 Question 3(c) asked for all three antibody diversity mechanisms, one mark each, with the command "Name precisely". There is no partial credit for naming the neighbouring mechanism, and a school examiner's report puts the penalty in one line: recombination and hypermutation earn nothing in a class-switching question. Question 4 is that specimen question in full, at its real marks, with the distinguishing drills built around it.

Question 4(e) is designed to punish an error in your own notes. It is your school's own 2024 Paper 1 Question 29, and its official key marks as true the statement that somatic hypermutation happens after the plasma cell has encountered antigen. Chapter 9.4 says the same thing twice, on printed pages 71 and 73. The specimen's own stem says activated B lymphocytes, and the correction is written out in that part's scheme. Answer the school's paper with the school's key, then read why you must never write it that way in prose.

Antibody gene rearrangement is filed here, not in Book 2. The Book 2 question bank files it under Control of Gene Expression. Somatic recombination, hyper-mutation and class switching all belong to Extension Topic A LO (d), and Specimen P3 Q3(c) proves it by asking for all three inside a Book 3 stem-cell question.

Question 2 is the full-cycle question, eleven marks running clonal selection, through clonal expansion, differentiation and antibody secretion, to a secondary response read off a real graph. Answer (a) to (c) as one story.

Three real figures, and honesty about the rest. Q1 carries 9477 Specimen Paper 1 Question 29's own diagram, Q4 carries 9477 Specimen Paper 3 Figure 3.2, and Q2 carries your school's 2025 Paper 3 Figure 1.5, all lifted from the papers themselves. Every other figure comes from a paper whose PDF is not in the papers, so the question carries that paper's own printed description rather than a redrawing, and says so on the page.

Cumulative over Cluster 1 and Books 1 to 8. Q3(a) and Q3(b) need protein structure from Book 1, down to quaternary structure and the bonds that hold it. Q4(f) is a genome arithmetic question and Q5(b) is a gene-locus diagram, both Book 2. Q2(a) needs mitosis from Book 3 named as the mechanism of clonal expansion. Q8 needs the whole fluid mosaic model from Book 1. Cluster 1's antigen, antigen presentation and dendritic cell are assumed throughout.

What the marks reward. An antibody has an antigen-binding site, never an active site, and a marker's note records that even "binding site" alone was not accepted. Disulfide bonds hold the four chains together; they never hold antigen to antibody. Write both structure and function, because a scheme rejects variable region or heavy chain only. Make the cell, not the antibody, the subject of every diversity verb. Name the same antigen in every secondary-response answer, and never write "rapid" alone, which a scheme rejects for lacking the comparison with the primary response.

Two further errors in your notes are corrected in the schemes here. Q2(a) carries the correction to printed page 34, which defines clonal selection as the mitosis. Q6(a) carries the correction to printed page 35, which has cytotoxic T cells killing with hydrogen peroxide.

One primary concept each, checked for duplicated required answers and not only duplicated labels. Q1 telling the cells apart by what they carry and what they do · Q2 the whole adaptive cycle from selection to secondary response · Q3 antibody structure paired to function, and the three classes weighed · Q4 the three diversity mechanisms named precisely from their effects · Q5 where the diversity comes from at the DNA level, and self-tolerance · Q6 MHC, presentation and cell-mediated killing · Q7 the two-by-two immunity grid argued through two real cases · Q8 the whole immune response argued from membranes.

Where two questions touch the same mechanism they need different paragraphs. Q4 asks you to name a mechanism from a described effect at one mark each; Q5 asks you to describe the recombination mechanism off a gene-locus diagram, ending at conformation. Q2(c) owns the primary-against-secondary explanation with data quoting; Q7 owns the immunity grid and never asks for the secondary response again. Q3 owns antibody structure; Q8 owns membrane structure and never repeats an antibody structural point.

Nothing from Cluster 3, and no viral replication cycle. Vaccination, herd immunity, smallpox, influenza and HIV damage mechanisms, tuberculosis, antibiotics, R0 and the epidemiology terms are all Cluster 3. No question here sets a viral or bacterial replication cycle, which belongs to Core Idea 2 LOs 2(e) and 2(g) in Book 4.
